main.job: identity: what or who someone or something is (name, job, origin, description)
main.why: Half of 'to be'; nothing gets said without it.

main.job: location and how someone or something is right now
main.why: Other half of 'to be'; the ser/estar split is the first big trap.
Only way to say something exists; invariable, very high frequency.

main.job: negation: no goes right before the verb (and stays with nada, nadie, nunca)
main.why: Negation job; the double-negative rule trips English speakers.

main.job: want (a thing or to do something)
main.why: Want job; also the everyday polite request form quiero / quisiera.

main.job: can / be able to / be allowed to
main.why: Can job; also the standard way to ask for things (¿puedo…?, ¿me puedes…?).
Must job; the everyday obligation construction.

main.job: going to: plans and the near future
main.why: Go job plus the easiest future; spoken Spanish uses it more than the future tense.

main.job: saying you like something (the thing is the subject: me gusta / me gustan)
main.why: Unlocks likes and dislikes; the structure is backwards for English speakers.

main.job: so / then: linking what happened to what comes next or follows
main.why: Top discourse connector in conversation; used to move a story or conclusion forward.

spares.job: have (possession) and age, hunger, cold with tener
spares.why: Have job; tener hambre / tener 20 años are unavoidable.
Reason connector; learners mix it with por qué.

spares.job: I mean / in other words: rephrasing mid-conversation
spares.why: Constant in real conversation; recognizing it helps follow speech.

jobs_covered.questions: yes/no questions use rising intonation on a normal sentence, no term needed; question words (qué, dónde, cuándo, cómo, cuánto, quién, cuál, por qué) are a closed set too big for count 10, so not started
jobs_covered.referring to people / politeness: subject pronouns incl. tú vs usted are a 9-member closed set, too big for count 10; verb endings carry the person, so not started
jobs_covered.have: spare s01 tener (cut by count; tener que covers the most urgent job)

shape.notes: Bare slice at A2–B1: building blocks and two unlocking constructions first, one glue item, no A1 content nouns or greetings. Pronoun and question-word sets deferred whole rather than started (R-SEL-04).
